chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, about a gazelle entering the Haram, and he said:
"It is not to be taken, nor touched, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"

key_terms.آمِنًا: safe and secure under the sanctuary's protection
key_terms.الظَّبْيِ: a gazelle, the specific animal mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the Sacred Sanctuary, whose precincts carry inviolable protection
key_terms.لَا يُؤْخَذُ: it must not be taken or captured
key_terms.لَا يُمَسُّ: it must not be touched or disturbed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a gazelle that enters the Haram in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the sanctity of the Haram: even a gazelle that enters it must not be seized or disturbed. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the Qur'anic principle that whoever enters the sanctuary is granted safety.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2368 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked one of the Imams (as)  about a gazelle entering the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram).
Imam (as) replied: "It should not be taken or touched because Allah (swt), the Almighty, says:
'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"
